architect.statement: I view architecture as a dialogue between people and space — where creativity meets purpose. As a learner, I design with curiosity, precision, and empathy, aiming to create spaces that evoke emotion and lasting memories. My goal is to shape meaningful, human-centered designs that inspire and endure.

projects.title: Mass Housing
projects.typology: High-rise mass housing with podium parking and retail

area_dimensions.terrace_levels_m: about +130.45 (D, E and F wings) to +145.45 (A, B and C wings), read from sections and elevations

projects.description: The site sits near one of the busiest roads in South Mumbai, where it meets Saat Rasta, so the project includes retail shops. The site has views in every direction, so making use of views was a priority. Instead of one large podium, two podiums are provided, which keeps the built footprint small and leaves the most ground open. A central recreational space is enclosed by the towers around it, giving it good airflow and privacy. Wings D, E and F are physically connected to get the desired form. The inspiration is Future Towers, Amanora Township, Pune.
key_facts: Design progression in four stages. Stage 1 had 8 towers around a central space on the ground. Stage 2 divided the podium for access and opened the centre. Stage 3 formed a more open layout. In the final stage the number of towers was reduced and a large central open space was designed with a minimum footprint.
Climate: tropical wet and dry, with heavy rain from June to September. Wind path from south-west to north-east.
Three basements and six podium levels of parking.
Podium-top amenities include a gym, spa, library and reading area, indoor games, kids' and elderly areas, swimming pool, kids' pool, deck and bridge.
Ground level holds a multipurpose area, amphitheatre, waterbody, basketball, tennis and badminton courts, and a cricket turf.
projects.notes: The final number of towers is not stated. Wings A to F appear on the drawings.

projects.title: Residential School
projects.location: Kanoi village, 35 km from Jaisalmer, Rajasthan
projects.typology: Educational campus: residential school with hostels and staff housing

area_dimensions.site_levels_m: contour bands from below 149 to above 173
area_dimensions.academic_block_levels_m: first ground floor at 161, last ground-floor level at 167

projects.description: The site has a lake that is a major source of water for the village and a gathering place where the village mela happens. Because water is scarce, the design keeps the lake from being affected or polluted by construction and slightly enlarges it for water retention and views. Different levels follow the natural contours instead of flattening a large area, without breaking the flow of space. Ramps and lifts make it universally accessible. Blocks use wind direction and sun path for daylight and natural ventilation. Courtyards and jalis aid ventilation. Space is left between structures so rainwater can flow to the lake. The academic block allows future expansion. Pathways connect all spaces with no dark or unsafe corners.
key_facts: Masterplan components: 1 security cabin, 2 auditorium, 3 entrance and admin block, 4 multipurpose hall, 5 academic block, 6 library and laboratories, 7 indoor games block, 8 playground, 9 mess, 10 boys' hostel, 11 faculty accommodation, 12 girls' hostel, 13 director's accommodation, 14 deputy director's accommodation, 15 amphitheatre, 16 parking, 17 lake.

Admin block: a ground-storey structure on three levels expressing a hierarchy. The principal's office is at the top, the admin office in the middle, and the entrance zone with display area and cafeteria at the bottom.
Academic block: G+1 on several levels following the contours. Inspired by Smritivan Earthquake Museum, Bhuj. Rajasthani style gives it the look of a fort.
Library and laboratories: G+1 in front of the academic block, stepping from 159 m to 157 m, with a ramp as its main feature and the feel of a basement.
Indoor sports block: G+1 at the centre of the site with a badminton court courtyard, stepped seating toward the playground usable as an amphitheatre, and studios for dance, drama and painting.
Mess: ground storey in a mixed Rajasthani and modern style, planned around students' daily routine, with a service driveway.

SWOT. Strengths: rich culture, unique local architecture, community involvement, local material. Weaknesses: harsh climate, water scarcity, limited infrastructure. Opportunities: sustainable design, educational empowerment, cultural preservation, tourism. Threats: climate change, environmental degradation, socio-economic disparity.

projects.title: Sukoon Resort
projects.semester: Semester 5 (Architectural Design), Sir J.J. College of Architecture

area_dimensions.site_area: 22.55 acres (label partly legible on p17; verify)

projects.description: The architect's statement: "My dream is to spend my vacation where my stay will be in village. I like the early morning sunlight, I like to walk in village, I love to talk to people and to do group activities." The resort incorporates these through gardens, sit-outs and an amphitheatre, and common open spaces between accommodation blocks. There are two residential zones. One is exposed to interactive public spaces. The other is quieter and private, with villas. Open structures are designed without disturbing privacy, with breathing space between buildings and similar structures clubbed together. The aim is to give the user the feel of Sukoon.
key_facts: Concept: voids between structures for visual connection to the surroundings. Light and shadow through terracotta jalis for privacy and visual connection. Courtyard planning for daylight and to keep interiors cool.
Inspirations: stepped garden and amphitheatre near a waterfront.

Programme: parking, reception, multipurpose area, cafe, two restaurants, guest villas, dormitories, archery, guest rooms, guest suites, badminton and tennis courts, sit-out space, multipurpose garden, service block, amphitheatre, stepped garden, deck, gym and indoor games, spa, changing area, common swimming pool, and an amphitheatre (kund).
Villa: 4BHK, G+1, on the edge of the site with a private pool facing the dam.
Guest rooms: 48 in total, six per cluster, with views on both sides.
Dormitories: for 10 people, two clustered together. Suite rooms share a common courtyard space.
Multipurpose hall: octagonal, with a stage and a roof cavity to stay cool in summer.
Reception: open reception inspired by Anchaviyo Resort.
Restaurants: one on the lake front with a central courtyard and a dining deck. One on the east side with river and dam views.
Cafe: open, with bush partitions and a pergola roof under transparent acrylic sheet.

projects.title: Irshalpada Rehabilitation
projects.typology: Post-disaster rehabilitation housing and community spaces

area_dimensions.cluster: 4 plots: 2 ground+1 storey houses and 2 ground storey houses

materials: Lime layer on chicken mesh with waterproofing coat
projects.description: On 19 July 2023 a massive landslide struck Irshalwadi village in Raigad. Before designing, the team contacted survivors to understand their requirements and lifestyle. Their houses were mostly brick, wattle and daub, with Mangalore tile roofs and stone plinths. Toilets were in the front or back yard and not part of the house. The residents are very social and closely connected to nature. The aim is to build a "home" where survivors feel as comfortable as before the landslide, one that does not hinder their ways of living but enhances them.
key_facts: Clusters of 4 houses form a central community space between them.
A primary school serves as a community space, with a big open ground and a stage for gram panchayat meetings, marriages and gatherings.
The "Temple of Memories" is a memorial stone to remember those who lost their lives, and a community space to reflect on the past.
Each house has a central courtyard connecting all rooms, many openings for light and ventilation, a retained traditional verandah, and a place for the traditional chul.
Toilets are kept apart from the house but on the same plinth, considering the rainfall.
Materials match the residents' old houses so they do not feel alienated.
Climate: hottest months March and April, maximum rainfall in July until mid-September, wind mainly from the south-west.

projects.title: Sales Office – Interior Design
projects.typology: Commercial interior: sales office and show flat
projects.client: Shreepati Developers (named in the design brief)
projects.description: The interior design of a sales office for Shreepati Developers' upcoming project, with a reception, discussion area, AV room, director's cabin, sales cabins, admin office, toilet, pantry and storage. The theme is "Lines", expressed through fluted panels that create rhythm and continuity. Placing and cutting the panels in different ways makes different linear patterns on walls and elevations. The same theme carries into the show flat, which communicates the design language of the builder's project. A white and off-white palette makes the spaces brighter and larger. All windows are fixed glazing with air-conditioning. The passage avoids a static, "dead" corridor. The front facade also echoes the lines, carrying the theme from exterior to interior and reinforcing the builder's brand identity.
key_facts: Hand-drawn and rendered sheets: front elevation, RCP, flooring layout, plan, perspectives and sections A-A' to F-F'.
projects.notes: Sheets are embedded at 72 ppi. Location and area are not stated.

projects.title: Dharavi Rerooted
projects.typology: Urban redevelopment: SRA rehabilitation and saleable housing
projects.description: A redevelopment proposal across Dharavi's sectors with a clear spatial split between SRA and saleable units. This gives dignity and autonomy to both. Saleable units face inward around their own common areas. SRA blocks have their own identity, open spaces and circulation cores, with no shared entries. Buffer zones of landscape, service roads or amenities reinforce the separation. Plus-shaped towers are arranged around community courtyards, and anganwadis and community centres sit in the courtyards to bring care, learning and togetherness to the heart of the community.
key_facts: Planning principles: versatility, adaptability, adaptability for future changes, efficient modular layout, easy-to-assemble building blocks, smart orientation, and common spaces and courtyards for a walkable neighbourhood.
Full-slit sliding windows reduce lintel and construction cost and increase light and ventilation.
Bison panel partitions save about 45–50% in cost against 150 mm brick partitions, build faster and add layout flexibility. Stated: ₹5,500–6,100 vs ₹10,300–11,800 for 8.25 sq m.
Maintenance: one building with 4 lifts instead of two buildings with 6 lifts. A corpus fund is stated at ₹40,000 per flat per annum, held in a fixed deposit controlled by BMC.
Units include loft provision, a jali wall and partitions residents can modify. The sheet also carries the theme "Empowering women in each household".
